We use our platform on Tufts' campus to uplift marginalized voices, hold institutions accountable, and showcase student work. The Observer intends to use journalism as a space for advocacy, community, and expression.

name: Office for Campus Life
description: The Office for Campus Life at Tufts University seeks to build community and inspire the growth of the whole student through a support system of guidance, compassion, service, and leadership. Our office, located in the Mayer Campus Center, fosters the growth and development of students in the areas of leadership and self-governance, and assists students in planning and coordinating a broad range of social, cultural, and educational programs.

name: Office of the Provost & Senior Vice President
description: The Office of the Provost is responsible for setting and advancing institutional priorities that support the university’s mission as a student-centered R1 institution. The office champions academic excellence across its education, research, and civic engagement missions while fostering the success of students, faculty, and staff. Through strategic leadership, collaboration, and coordination, the office strengthens the university's academic enterprise and advances innovation, impact, and institutional effectiveness.

name: Onero Institute
description: The Onero Institute is a youth-driven, nonprofit research organization that seeks to develop the next generation of leaders and global affairs experts by bridging the divide between young people and the professional community and by creating an intergenerational space that elevates the role of youth in engaging with international issues.

name: ONYX Magazine
description: The mission of Onyx Magazineis to "expose the power and beauty of Black expression in its purest literary form," creating a safe space for artists on campus to freely express themselves and hone their passions.

name: Optics Research Club
description: To facilitate discussion of optics research between students

name: Organization of Graduate Students in Mathematics
description: OGSM is a graduate student organization committed to organizing and advocating on behalf of and in the interests of masters and doctoral students at Tufts University in the Department of Mathematics.

name: Orientation & Student Experience
description: We assist students and families to understand the expectations and opportunities of the Tufts community. We help prepare students for their academic and co-curricular journeys by facilitating an introduction to their peers and to Tufts’ services.

name: Origami Club
description: Our mission is to spread the art and culture of origami and papermaking. The club encourages artistic expression, collaboration on projects and exhibitions, mentorship for novice members, and innovation in techniques and materials.

name: Orthodox Christian Fellowship
description: The Orthodox Christian Fellowship transforms the lives of college students by guiding them along the path to Jesus Christ through His Church, cultivating a campus community of worship, witness, service, fellowship, and education.

name: Pakistani Association for Graduate Students
description: To build community and support networks between incoming, current and previous Pakistani graduate students at Tufts.

name: Pan-Afrikan Alliance
description: The Pan-Afrikan Alliance (PAA) aims to stimulate the political consciousness of Black students at Tufts regarding socio-political happenings on and beyond campus through events, meetings, and multimedia engagements

name: Parnassus
description: To foster a collective of writers, artists, and other creative members of the Tufts community, emphasizing the creative process over the product.

name: Partners In Health ENGAGE
description: To mobilize students in support of the global movement for health equity and the belief that healthcare is a fundamental human right

name: Pediatric Hope Project
description: The Pediatric Hope Project provides free, one-on-one virtual tutoring for students who are in treatment for, or recovering from, pediatric cancer and other life-threatening medical conditions.

name: Pen Pals
description: Mission of our club is to foster the English language learning of Somerville middle school students who are a part of their school's ESL (English as a Second Language), SEI (Shelter English Immersion), or SLIFE (Students with Limited or Interrupted Formal Education) . Tufts students write letters to middle school students at Winter Hill every 2 weeks (we are planning to expand this program to other schools). This program has been incorporated in the English and Language Arts curriculum at Winter Hill. Our mission is to connect Tufts Students (who come form a more privileged education backgroun

name: Pen, Paint, & Pretzels
description: Throughout its history, Pen, Paint and Pretzels has provided a diverse community of Tufts students with the opportunity to participate in all aspects of theatre production. 3Ps focuses on creating a supportive environment that fosters innovative and exciting works. We maintain a close working relationship with the Tufts Department of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies (TDPS), which provides our theatre artists/makers with the educational support needed to help them develop their craft. We also facilitate communication among our many affiliate student performance organizations in order to

name: Pep Band
description: Have fun playing good tunes to bring pep to the fans.

name: PERIOD @ Tufts (LCS)
description: PERIOD is a global youth-run nonprofit that strives to end menstrual inequity and stigma through service, education, and advocacy. We welcome people of all backgrounds to help us further serve not only our Tufts community, but also underserved communities in the greater Boston area and around the world. PERIOD @ Tufts is always open to collaborations and encourages the inclusion of different perspectives.

name: Persian Student Association
description: We believe that Tufts University is a very diverse university filled with many students with different backgrounds and we aim to gather all students that are interested in different cultures in our club. We will educate, share and promote our cultural events, creating a close knit community that share similar values.

name: Petey Greene Program
description: The Petey Greene Program envisions a world in which all incarcerated people have access to high-quality academic programs and we strive to inspire our alumni - both students and tutors - to become advocates, and to take on leadership roles that reimagine the criminal legal system.

name: Phi Alpha Delta
description: Phi Alpha Delta is the world’s preeminent law fraternity because of our dedication to service: service to the student, the school, the profession, and the community. It is through devotion to the ideals of compassion, courage, diversity, innovation, integrity, professionalism, and service that we better both our profession and our community. Through accepting our differences we become not just a law fraternity, but a family.

name: Philippine Student Union
description: The Philippine Student Union strives to foster solidarity within the Filipinx community at Tufts, explore our relationship with Philippine culture and history, promote an intentional space for the celebration and education of Philippine culture, and bring awareness of the Philippines’s contribution to the Asian/Southeast Asian diaspora.

name: Pickleball (Club Sport)
description: Tufts Club Pickleball fosters an inclusive community where players of all skill levels can enjoy the sport. Our mission is to provide a welcoming environment for both recreational and competitive play, promoting sportsmanship, camaraderie, and personal growth

name: Planned Parenthood Action at Tufts
description: To develop and sustain a grassroots constituency that uses the political process to guarantee everyone the right to make personal decisions regarding the full range of reproductive choices, including preventing unintended pregnancy; bearing healthy children; and choosing safe, legal, accessible abortion.

name: Pole Collective
description: We aim to promote fitness and creative expression through pole dance accessible to all while educating students about the history and cultural significance of this artform.

name: Pre-Dental Society
description: To provide undergraduate students interested in a career in dentistry with ample resources.

name: Pre-Health Post-Baccalaureate Society
description: Encourage the curiosity of career changers towards a variety of specialties and health professions

name: Pre-Law Society
description: With no specific pre-law track for undergraduate students, the Tufts Pre-Law Society helps students who have an interest in the legal profession and legal issues by gathering a group of like-minded individuals with many overlapping ideas and concerns. Many of our members are troubled by the fact that a pre-law student has much flexibility in their undergraduate career. One of our main goals therefore, is to help our members take advantage of all of the opportunities offered to them.

name: Pre-Medical Society
description: To provide necessary resources and advice for students on the pre-medical track, to help build a community of support for aspiring pre-medical students and to provide students with a sense of what a career in medicine looks like beyond Tufts.

name: Pre-Physician Assistant Society
description: The core goal of Pre-Physician Assistant Society is to share and spread knowledge to those interested in the Physician Assistant profession, as well as ensure that all graduate school prerequisites are met.

name: Pre-Veterinary Society
description: To provide resources and opportunities for students considering veterinary medicine as a future career and to raise funds for animal-affiliated nonprofit organizations.

name: Prison Initiative
description: The Tufts University Prison Initiative of the Tisch College of Civic Life (TUPIT) brings Tufts faculty and students together with incarcerated and formerly incarcerated people, corrections staff, educators, and scholars of criminal justice to facilitate creative and collaborative responses to the problems of mass incarceration. Extending the vision of Tufts University and Tisch College, TUPIT is dedicated to providing transformative educational experiences that foster students’ and faculty members’ capacities to become active citizens of change in the world.

name: Product Studio
description: A student-led organization building a community around exciting products while inspiring innovation and love for tech.

name: Project Car Club
description: PCC provides all undergraduate students, regardless of major or prior experience, with hands-on education and transferable experience in real-world automotive mechanics, diagnostics, and garage/workshop safety through collaborative maintenance and workshops on a dedicated production vehicle.

name: Project Linus (LCS)
description: Our mission is to support children who are ill, traumatized, or otherwise in need of some love and comfort through the gifts of handmade blankets.

name: Project SHARE
description: Project SHARE aims to reduce disparities among Tufts and local communities by advancing access to health care, and providing resources and education in support of the universal right to health.​

name: Project Sunshine (LCS)
description: Project Sunshine is a multi-national, volunteer-based nonprofit that meets the social-emotional needs of pediatric patients and families living with all medical challenges. Project Sunshine's mission is to bring joy and play to pediatric patients.

name: Protestant Student Association
description: We are a progressive Protestant community that seeks to serve the greater Tufts community and each other in worship, outreach, and fellowship.

name: Psychology Society

name: Public Harmony

name: Pulse

name: Questbridge Scholars

We wish to provide "a thriving community and transformative educational, career, and life opportunities [to] help propel students [in hopes of living] lives of fulfillment, meaning, and purpose. QuestBridge seeks to create a more equitable society where every student can dream big, reach their potential, contribute to the world, and build a life that they love."

name: Quiz Bowl

name: Real Estate Society

name: RealTalk

name: Red Cross Club

name: Returning Student Organization
description: The RSO exists to support nontraditional and adult learners at Tufts by fostering community, sharing resources, and ensuring members feel connected and supported within the university.

name: Robotics Club
description: Our mission is to build practical skills by being hands on with real robots. We aim to empower all our members to learn new skills and tackle new challenges.

name: Roti and Rum
description: The mission of ROTI & RUM is to represent Tufts University, displaying the quality and caliber of performance-based student groups of Tufts University, at all performance-based events, and to embark on all opportunities that allow said group to do so. Our goal as a group is to embrace all aspects and influence of the Caribbean culture by dancing to a variety of music such as Soca, Dembow, Reggae, Dancehall, etc...

name: Roundnet Club

name: Rugby (Men's Club Sport)
description: The TURFC is dedicated to building sportsmanship and camaraderie among our passionate members and promoting the great sport of Rugby on and around the Tufts campus.

name: Rugby (Women's Club Sport)
description: Tufts Women’s Rugby Football Club was established in 1978 and has grown to a considerable presence on campus since then. This club sport is a competitive team that participates in the NEWCRC conference small college league. TWRFC is centered in teaching rugby to those interested in a new sport, regardless of skill level or past history. Being a player on the team is a fantastic way to play a competitive sport while also having a great community on campus.

name: Running Club (Club Sport)
description: The mission of TURC is to create a supportive environment for students to become better runners, compete regionally and nationally with other club teams, and have fun while doing so!

name: S-Factor
description: Founded in 2006, S-Factor is dedicated to spreading black music throughout Tufts and off campus areas. S-Factor commits to providing entertainment as well as educating audience members about this rich musical culture.

name: Salon Soiree (SMFA)
description: Our focus is to provide pre-professional and networking opportunities for art history interested students. Events we have in mind are setting up a networking night, inviting Tufts/SMFA alumni in the museum/art fields to speak to current students, and inviting recruiters from local museums/ galleries to speak and share opportunities available with interested students. We believe there is an unrecognized potential at Tufts for student artists, curators and aspiring preparators and through this club we believe we can harness this very potential and develop it to make our community more vibrant.

name: Sarabande Dance Ensemble
description: Our mission is to bring dance to the Tufts community while continuing to grow as dancers and choreographers.

Our members plan and run every part of the tournament, from writing and administering events to supervising, grading, and setup, gaining hands-on experience organizing a large STEM event while earning meaningful community service and outreach hours. name: SEDS: Students for the Exploration and Development of Space
description: To create and nurture an aerospace-minded community at Tufts, while developing technical proficiency and professional capability.

Through our podcast, Instagram account, and in-person programming, we work to educate the Tufts undergraduate community about sexual health, consent, and healthy relationships. description: In Shir Appeal, we like to say that we are Jewish by our music, not our membership. Our members come from a wide variety of backgrounds to sing and record albums together, showcasing the beauty and variety of Jewish music. We believe that sharing our music not only brings joy to so many, but also makes Jewish music accessible and creates a k’ehillah (community!).

name: Shotokan Karate (Club Sport)
description: We hope to introduce you to the world of martial arts. Karate is a great calisthenic workout and a fun way to interact with other students.

name: SMFA Print Club

name: SMFA Student Government Association
description: Our mission as the School of the Museum of Fine Arts Student Government Association (SGA) is to serve as the representational, active voice for the student body and to improve students’ intellectual and social life through programs, events, and policy. SGA works in open communication with SMFA faculty, staff, and administration to uphold a safe, inclusive, and respectful community environment.

name: Smiles for All
description: Our mission is to make dental care more accessible and less anxious for children with developmental disabilities, including autism spectrum disorder, Down syndrome, and cerebral palsy. We do this through our Comfort Companionship program, as well as our community education program.

name: Soccer (Men's Club Sport)
description: Tufts men's club soccer plays to enjoy the sport of soccer, build a team atmosphere for students on campus, and allow driven soccer players to find competitive success.

name: Soccer (Women's Club Sport)
description: Have fun and play soccer!

name: Social Event Registration Committee
description: The mission of the Social Event Registration Committee is to promote safe, responsible, and well-managed social events by reviewing and approving event registrations, providing Student Life Risk Management Workshops, and maintaining and updating policies and guidelines for social events involving alcohol. Social Event Registration Form: https://cglink.me/28v/s45

name: Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics
description: Bring invited speakers from industry and other STEM departments and fields to talk about their experiences and research.

SWE aims to be a key to the success of women in engineering and technology. Members of the organization aspire to the highest level of ethical behavior with honesty and dignity in both their personal and professional relationships and responsibilities. Our mission is rooted in promoting pan-Latinx political consciousness and solidarity amongst the student body, as well as connecting students to resources and opportunities beyond Tufts.

name: Stand-Up Comedy Collective
description: The Stand Up Comedy Collective’s (SUCC) overall mission is to cultivate a group of collaborative, hilarious stand up comedians by holding weekly meetings during which interested students can practice their stand up acts by performing and then getting feedback from other members. SUCC aims to put on two primary shows per semester as well as occasional additional performances and open mic nights open to the Tufts community.

description: Provide opportunities for students to observe the night sky through telescopes and other equipment. Learn about astronomy, space science, and recent discoveries (including from telescopes like JWST). Encourage curiosity, critical thinking, and appreciation for the natural universe. Foster a community of students interested in stargazing, science outreach, and astronomical discovery.

name: Student Garden
description: Our mission is to create a happy and stress-free environment that fosters promotion of gardening and homesteading activities around campus. We also want to increase the awareness of food insecurity on college campuses and provide more ways for students to access nutritious food.

name: Student Occupational Therapy Association
description: SOTA represents the body of graduate student interests within our department and Tufts University. Our aim is to organize and advocate for student interests and concerns, while enhancing the growth of the students, the university at large, and the community. SOTA is concerned with promoting occupational therapy through university and community outreach.

name: Students Demand Action at Tufts University

We hope to achieve this through political engagement such as lobby days, letter writing, and public advocacy initiatives.

name: Students of Turkey
description: Tufts Students of Turkey (TSOFT) is an association that builds community among people of Turkey by providing an inclusive social space at Tufts and in the greater Boston area and aims to promote the multifaceted culture and history of Turkey to the wider Tufts community.

description: We are the Sub-Saharan Africa Research Group, a student-led organization at Tufts dedicated to promoting discourse on all things Africa (cultural, social, political, historical, economic issues, etc). This will be achieved through discussion sessions, conferences, conversations with guest lecturers, collaboration with like-minded student groups, and research trips to Sub-Saharan Africa. name: Supporting Women in Finance at Tufts
description: Supporting Women in Finance at Tufts (S.W.I.F.T.) is dedicated to creating a supportive community where students can explore careers in finance, develop technical and leadership skills, and connect with peers and professionals. Through mentorship, education, and professional development, we aim to equip members with knowledge, confidence, and connections, to become the next generation of leaders in finance, while advancing the representation of women across the industry.

name: Surf Club

name: SURGE: Sino-U.S. Relations Group Engagement

description: Our goal is to promote watching and competing in the CBS show 'Survivor'. This includes hosting a student adaptation of the show where participants compete in various competitions and outlast their teammates until a winner is chosen. We plan to host events related to the show and create a positive environment for those interested in this show.

name: SustainableCORE Fellows
description: SustainableCORE (Cultivating our Resilient Environment) Fellows foster a culture of sustainability at Tufts by engaging in inclusive community building that emphasizes sustainable action, equity, and celebration. As a cohort, the SustainableCORE Fellows serve as a bridge, connecting the mission of the Office of Sustainability to the larger Tufts community.

We seek to empower all of our members in their pursuits of their passions/interests, to create a social, supportive space that is welcoming and safe to all, and to foster an environment that promotes values such as community service, inclusion, scholarship, and professional development. name: The Africana Center
description: The Africana Center was founded in 1969 in response to student activism and the recognized needs of students of African descent. It fosters a supportive environment for students' personal, social, and academic development through a range of programs and resources. Serving as a vital gathering space for Tufts University students and community members, the Center encourages learning, shared experiences, mutual support, and the celebration of the diverse cultures within the African diaspora. name: The Experimental College
description: The Experimental College is a department at Tufts University that offers innovative undergraduate elective courses. We hire Visiting Lecturers with a range of perspectives and professional experience to teach interdisciplinary, interactive courses. At the ExCollege, students can design and teach courses, serve on our governing board, evaluate course proposals, interview prospective Visiting Lecturers, select courses to be offered, and more!

name: The Office of Religious and Philosophical Life
description: The Office of Religious and Philosophical Life is a dynamic hub supporting religious, spiritual, ethical, and cultural life for all members of the Tufts community. Our primary mission is to: To provide spiritual care To support religious and philosophical communities To educate about spiritual and ethical issues in society and the world Promote multifaith engagement.

name: Theta Chi Fraternity
description: Founded on the principle of brotherhood through the mutual assistance of every member, Theta Chi aims to provide its members with an enjoyable and fulfilling collegiate experience that also prepares them for rewarding, successful lives after graduation.

name: Thirst Project (LCS)

name: THREAD: Tufts Harm Reduction Education for Alcohol and Drugs
description: We acknowledge that although drug use has risks associated with it, it will and does continue to happen. Thus, our mission is to help people who are going to use substances anyway minimize their risk of harm by educating them and offering protective resources (ex: narcan). We believe that all humans are deserving of autonomy, respect, safety, and care, whether or not they use substances.

name: Timmy Global Health
description: Timmy Global Health expands access to healthcare and empowers students and volunteers to tackle today’s most pressing global health challenges.

Our students are acutely aware of the need to cultivate and promote international understanding and they are hungry to engage as global citizens.

name: Tufts for Health Equity
description: We aim to strengthen the movement for global health equity by empowering students and communities to work together to improve the health of all around the world. This collaboration allows for the rational design of projects to both disseminate knowledge and provide basic healthcare to improve the lives of those people living in the partner community. Tufts for Health Equity strives to take a sustainable approach through learning about challenges in healthcare and working consistently with our partner organization.

name: Tufts Global Education
description: Tufts Global Education is committed to providing transformative, intercultural experiences to students-encouraging them to engage in the world with curiosity, to approach new challenges with innovation, and to distinguish themselves as responsible, active citizens of the world.

name: Tufts Graduate Robotics Association
description: The Tufts Graduate Robotics Association’s mission is to foster an interdisciplinary community of graduate students in robotics by promoting collaboration, intellectual exchange, and engagement with emerging research and technologies across academia and industry.

name: Tufts Student Alumni Collective

name: TURBO
description: Turbo strives to enrich and expand Tufts' culture through break dancing/hip-hop dance. We want to create a healthy and accepting community for our members and encourage everyone to express themselves.

name: Tutoring (LCS)
description: LCS Tutoring is a tutoring program that aids students in the surrounding Medford and Boston area in all subjects ranging from math to language. Tutoring is available for all kids from 1st to 12th grade. All tutoring occurs in person on Tufts campus or virtually, and the program uses Tufts volunteers who specialize in subjects such as calculus, Spanish, and much more.

name: TUTV: Tufts University Television
description: Tufts University Television (TUTV) is a student-run production studio. We strive to foster a supportive and collaborative community where anyone can develop their own artistic voice through creating their very own films and television shows! With a focus on self-paced learning, students can learn about the filmmaking and television production process as well as the media and entertainment industries. name: Urban Studies Club
description: The Urban Studies Club seeks to create a community for all those interested in urban studies, planning, design, transportation, and related fields, and the impacts they have on society. These interests are to be channeled into club projects and advocacy to benefit the community's progressive development of urban life, including infrastructure, housing, public spaces, and more.

description: Educates Tufts undergraduates on the fundamental of venture capital. Conducts projects for venture capital firms tailored to their needs by leveraging analyst manpower, perspective, and business acumen.

description: We strive to introduce and promote the Vietnamese culture to the Tufts community through cultural, educational, and social events relating to our Vietnamese heritage both on and off campus. We also hope to be a source of support for all Vietnamese-identified students on campus by organizing more inclusive events that are relevant to the need of the Vietnamese community at Tufts.

name: Women in Electrical & Computer Engineering
description: Women in Electrical and Computer Engineering (WECE) is dedicated to advancing the success and well-being of individuals within the ECE department, with a focus on promoting gender equity. Our mission is to foster a supportive and inclusive environment through community-building, career development, and resource-sharing. Our commitment to inclusivity extends to all marginalized groups within the department, who are encouraged to engage in community-building and utilize our resources. Together, we work towards fostering an atmosphere of empowerment and opportunity for all.

name: Women in International Relations
description: To cultivate a community of globally-minded fem-identifying students looking to engage with real world issues, grow professionally, and explore the field.

name: Women in Medicine
description: WIM aims to create a space on Tufts’ campus to recognize and highlight the unique contributions of women in medicine throughout history and in the modern day, and the inequities within how women are treated as both providers and patients in the field of healthcare to increase overall health awareness in our community. In doing so, Women in Medicine hopes to foster an enriching and supportive environment for Tufts’ premed students to feel empowered to pursue careers in medicine and science.

name: Women in Product
